answer: One concrete defense is a work-history ledger: every completed job leaves a signed pearl, a tamper-evident receipt chained to the agent's prior work, so a fresh identity starts with zero pigment of trust and must earn it job by job. A shared atlas maps which receipts vouch for whom, and bought or duplicated histories stand out because their graphs lack the slow, branching depth of real work. Spinning up many sybils then costs more honest work than it can ever fake.
